  ### Deobfuscation Step 1 of 4 — inlineObjectProps                                                                                                                                                                     
  
  Technique: inlineObjectProps
  What happens: All alias variables that hold a reference to the decoder function are
  removed. Every call through the alias is replaced with a direct call to __DECODE_0__.

  Example:
    Before:
      var alias = __DECODE_0__;          ← alias declaration
      ...
      arr[alias(0x10)]                   ← call through alias

    After:
      arr[__DECODE_0__(0x10)]            ← alias removed, direct call restored

  Diff notation used below:
    N\        line N from the previous version is UNCHANGED (content omitted)
    -N: ...   line N is REMOVED
    +N: ...   new line inserted at position N in the result

Step 4 prompt (data_4 → data_5): Post-decode cleanup

  ### Deobfuscation Step 4 of 4 — Post-decode cleanup

  Technique: mergeStrings, deadCode, controlFlowObject, controlFlowSwitch
  What happens: Final cleanup passes are applied.
    - mergeStrings: adjacent string literals are concatenated
    - deadCode: unreachable branches are removed
    - controlFlowObject: dispatcher objects used for control-flow flattening are inlined
    - controlFlowSwitch: switch-based control-flow flattening is unrolled
  For programs that do not use these patterns, this step produces no changes and all
  lines pass through unchanged.

  Example (mergeStrings):
    -5:   x = "hel" + "lo";     ← split literals
    +5:   x = "hello";           ← merged

  Example (deadCode):
    -8:   if (false) { foo(); }  ← unreachable branch removed
    (line deleted entirely)

  Example (no changes — simple program):
    1\
    2\
    3\
    ...                           ← every line unchanged, only numbers listed

  Diff notation: N\ = unchanged, -N: = removed, +N: = added in result.
